It may also be employed in baths for electroplating of nickel, zinc, alloys etc and for alkaline cleaning. The salt is indus1. A-2.2 Procedure - Dissolve 50 g of the material, accurately weighed in about 400 ml of water in a 500 ml volumetric flask and make up to the mark. Pipette 50 ml portion of the solution into a 250 ml conical flask, add about 20 ml of water and a few drops of bromophenol blue indicator. Titrate the solution to a PH of 3.8 against 1 N hydrochloric acid taken in a burette. A change in colour of the solution from blue-violet to yellow denotes the end-point. A-4.1.3 Standard Chloride Sokion - Dissolve 0.33 g of dried sodium chloride or 0.421 g of potassium chloride in 1 litre volumetric flask and make up to the mark. Pipette 10 ml of the solution and dilute it to 1 000 ml in another volumetric flask. One millilitre of this solution contains 0.002 mg chloride ( as cl ). A-4.2 Procedure - Pipette out 10 ml of potassium pyrophosphate solution prepared for test ( See A-2.2 ) in a 50 ml Nessler cylinder, add 3 ml of concentrated nitric acid and 1 ml of silver nitrite solution. Dilute to 50 ml with water and mix well. Carry out a control test in another Nessler cylinder using 10 ml of standard chloride solution and the same quantities of other reagents. The material shall be taken as not having exceeded the limit prescribed in Table 1, if the turbidity produced with the material is not greater than that produced in the control test. A-5. A-9.3 Procedure - Pipette 20 ml of the solution prepared for test ( see A-2.2 ) into a 50 ml conical flask or test tube and add 1 g of ammonium nitrate. Warm the mixture to 40-45 "C and mix 5 ml of the same with the molybdate reagent. Shake the whole solution continuously for 10 minutes and allow to stand for 10 minutes. The intensity of yellow colout of the solution should not be greater than in the case of a standard solution containing 6 mg of orthophosphate and treated similarly.

A=19.3 Procedure - Pipette out 5U ml of solution prepared for test ( See A-2.2 ) into a 500 ml flat bottomed distilling flask carrying a thistle funnel and suitable attachments for steam-distillation. Add about 40 ml of dilute sulphuric acid and cooling the mixture of carbon dioxide and steam by cold water circulation in the condenser and receive the condensate in 20 ml of sodium hydroxide solution. Steam-distil for 30 minutes. Remove the vessel containing sodium hydroxide and carry out titration with standard hydrochloric acid solution first to phenolphthalein end-point and then to methyl orange end-point. A-10.4

APPENDIX ( Clause 4.1 )
SAMPLING B-l. GENERAL SAMPLING OF POTASSIUM OF PYROPHOSPHATE

B

FOR ELECTROPLATING

REQUIREMENTS

B-1.0 In drawing, preparing, storing and handling test samples, the following precautions and directions shall be observed. B-P.1 Precautions shall be taken to protect the samples, the material being sampled, the sampling i:lstrument and the containers for samples frorn adventitious contamination.
B-1.2 To draw a representative sample, the contents of each container selected for sampling shall IJ,C mixed as thoroughly as possible by suitable means.

B-2.3 All the containers shall be selected at random and in order to ensure the randomness of selection, procedures given in 1s : 4905-lW)* may be followed. B-3. TEST SAMPLES

AND

REFEREE

SAMPLE B-3.1 Preparation B-3.1.1 of Test Samples
Draw with an appropriate sampling instrument a small portion of the material from difl'erent parts of each container selected. The total quantity of the material drawn from eacll container shall be sufficient to conduct the tests for dll the characteristics given in 2 and shall not exceed 500 g. B-3.1.2 Thoroughly mix all portions of tile material drawn from the same container. Out of these portions a small but equal quantity shall be taken from each selected container and shall be well mixed up together so as to form a composite sample weighing not less than 200 g. Tllis composite sample shall be divided into three equal parts, one for the purchaser, second for the manufacturer and the third to be used as referee sample. B-3.1.3 The remaining portions of the material from each container ( after ;z small quantity needed for the formation of composite sample has been taken ) shall be divided into three equal not less than 50 g. parts, each part weighing These parts shall be immediately transferred to thoroughly dried bottles which arc: then sealed, air-tight with stoppers and labelled .with all the particulars of sampling given under B-1.4. Thr material in each such sealed bottle shall constitute an individual test sample. These il~dividual samples shall be separated into three identical sets of samples in such a way that eacll s1.t llas an individual test sample representing each container selected. One of thesc three sets shall br. sent to the purchaser, another to the manutlcturer atltl the third shall be used as referee salnple. B-3.2 Referee Sample - The referee sample composite sample ( sez of the shall consist samp!es ( ::tc B-3.1.2 ) and a set of individual B-3.1.3 ) marked for this purpose.
